experiment: Exact next-seat connector count conditional on opening forced pass after 1-1
conditioning: Starter owns 1-1, draws one stock tile, and has no other 1-x ordinary connector in the resulting nine-tile hand; six ordinary 1-x connectors are among 18 tiles split 9/9 between the two opponents.
method: Hypergeometric: P(K=k)=C(6,k)*C(12,9-k)/C(18,9). Independently computed in local Python 3 using math.comb.
new_finding: Conditional on the starter's forced opening pass, the next player has at least two ordinary 1-x connectors in 93.44% of deals; mean is exactly 3. This measures tile ownership, not guaranteed move legality, selected move, or strategic advantage.
confidence: Exact combinatorics under uniform deals and the confirmed opening condition; no engine validation or strategy inference.
limitations: Branch unlocking, block scoring, loneZero=10 provisional; connector ownership does not imply legal branch or optimal play. No full simulator checkout because executable git DNS fails.
validation: Local Python math.comb calculation executed; 0/17 gameplay and 0/4 hidden-world suites executed; 0 Monte Carlo worlds.
historical_baseline: 180000 persisted matched-seat rounds, separate and not combined with this exact enumeration.
next_action: Recover complete single-commit SHA/path/size-verified research-only checkout, run strict audit and preflight, 17 gameplay plus 4 hidden-world suites and fingerprint replays, archive raw outputs, then matched-seed strategy comparisons.
